title: Unfiltered customer voices + proposal lanes
body:
Purpose and framing:
This is a working dump of unfiltered customer feedback collected between 2026-01-10 and 2026-02-28 from support tickets, post-demo notes, account health calls, and two customer interviews. The goal is not to be polished: treat this as raw inputs for product ops and PMs to propose concrete lanes and quick experiments.

How this was assembled:
- Sources: 48 support threads tagged "latency" or "cost-optimization", 22 demo follow-ups, notes from two 1:1 interviews (enterprise customer in fintech, growth-stage startup in commerce), and a short CS triage meeting 2026-02-25.
- Method: verbatim highlights extracted, then grouped into informal buckets (no heavy weighting yet). Each bucket contains representative quote(s), suggested small experiment or proposal lane, and an initial (subjective) impact/effort sketch.

Guiding constraints for proposals: keep bandwidth low (ownerable within 2-4 sprints for quick wins), minimize infra-ops changes for early experiments, and prioritize items that reduce per-token cost or reduce P1 incidents.

Raw buckets (unfiltered) and representative quotes:
1) Request: Better per-route cost visibility and predictive estimates
Representative quotes:
- "We'd love a billable token forecast per endpoint — right now we guess based on calls and get surprises after spikes." (mid-market SaaS)
- "If I could see cost per prompt type, I could move expensive calls to a cheaper model automatically." (platform team)
Proposal lane: Per-route predicted spend; route-level budgets and soft caps.
Initial impact/effort: High impact for finance-conscious customers; medium effort (frontend + aggregation).

2) Request: Easier canary/fallback definitions for model variants (policy-as-config)
Representative quotes:
- "We want to test gpt-4-style models vs cheaper 7B variants for 10% of traffic and fall back automatically on latency or error signals." (enterprise)
- "Current rollouts require manual routing rules in two systems; it takes too long." (AI-startup)
Proposal lane: Tiny DSL in Console to define weight-based rollouts + threshold-based fallback (latency/error).
Initial impact/effort: High impact (reliability + cost); higher effort (console + control plane).

3) Request: Better prefix caching visibility and query patterns
Representative quotes:
- "We think much of our traffic shares prefixes but we can't prove it. If Redwood suggested prefixes to cache, that'd save a ton." (commerce customer)
Proposal lane: A batch job + console widget that shows top prefix clusters and estimated token-save if cached.
Initial impact/effort: Medium impact; low-to-medium effort (analytics job + UI).

4) Request: More predictable streaming semantics across SDKs
Representative quotes:
- "Different SDKs behave slightly differently under stream+reconnect; we had to implement client-side glue." (platform eng)
Proposal lane: Align SDK streaming spec and release a compatibility guide + small client helper library.
Initial impact/effort: Medium; low effort (engineering docs + small libs).

5) Request: Easier private deployment checklist and preflight tests
Representative quotes:
- "Private deployment is great but the preflight feels manual. A local-run checklist and smoke tests would have helped." (regulated customer)
Proposal lane: Add a "preflight-run" script + binary health checks + a standard smoke suite.
Initial impact/effort: Medium impact for enterprise; medium effort (ops + packaging).

6) Request: Granular rerank/explainability metrics for embeddings + reranking
Representative quotes:
- "When relevance drops, we need a per-query signal to tune our reranker." (search product)
Proposal lane: Add per-query reranker score deltas and a sampling tool that shows before/after rank lists.
Initial impact/effort: Medium-high; medium effort (instrumentation + tooling).

Representative quick wins (ownerable in 1 sprint each):
- Console: Add a small toggle to show 7-day spend trend for each route (frontend + call to existing accounting API).
- Docs: Publish a short streaming compatibility guide for major SDKs, include reconnection recipe and sample code.
- CS playbook: Create an enterprise preflight checklist template for Private deployments.

Big bets / mid-term lanes (2-3 months):
- Policy-as-config for model rollouts (requires control-plane changes, routing, and rollout UX).
- Prefix-suggestion cache optimizer (analytics + runtime cache integration).
- Per-route predictive budgeting with soft caps and notifications.

Initial triage rubric (simple, subjective) used in meeting: impact = {low|med|high}, effort = {low|med|high}, confidence = {low|med|high}. Items above are labeled accordingly in the buckets.

Open questions and unknowns (need data):
- What % of customers would enable an automatic fallback by latency vs by absolute error rate? Need a quick survey + product analytics query.
- For prefix caching: what is the current cache hit distribution by route? (run a sampling job).
- For per-route spend forecasting: can billing data be aggregated per route without a major schema change? (ask infra/billing).

Risks and countermeasures:
- Risk: Building rollout policy tooling too generic and delaying delivery. Countermeasure: ship a minimal, opinionated first version with a couple of preset policies (latency, cost).
- Risk: Prefix suggestions could surface privacy-sensitive strings. Countermeasure: do prefix suggestion only on aggregated/anonymized tokens and show examples after hash-masking.

Suggested next steps (owner + short timeline):
1) Product ops (Marcus Lee) to run a short internal survey to gauge appetite for automatic fallback (complete by 2026-03-12).
2) Engineering (SRE/Serving) to run two sampling jobs: per-route prefix hit distribution and per-route token attribution (estimate time: 2 weeks).
3) Console/FE (Sofia Nguyen) to ship the 7-day route spend toggle (sprint 1 quick win).
4) CS (Aisha Patel) to draft the Private preflight checklist and circulate to security/compliance for quick review (1 week).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally raw; don't edit quotes unless you verify against the source ticket.
- If a PM wants to pick up a lane, flag which quick-win you want to own so we can remove it from the "unowned" queue.

Appendix: random verbatim snippets (for tone)
- "Latency spikes every Thursday afternoon — we think it's batch jobs hitting the same model."
- "We'd trade a small accuracy drop for 30% cost savings on some endpoints."
- "The console is great — we just need the small knobs."

End of dump.
